# meshstack_building_block_runner (Data Source)

Read a single building block runner by UUID, defaulting to the shared runner meshStack hosts. Use it to configure the trust of a cloud backplane that exists before any building block definition — the shared AWS OIDC provider, a GCP workload identity pool provider — from `spec.workload_identity_federation.issuer` and the per-cloud `audience`.

Read the **subject** from the definition instead: `spec.workload_identity_federation.subject_template` is a template, and meshStack resolves it per building block definition into `meshstack_building_block_definition.<name>.status.workload_identity_federation.subject`. A module that grants a definition access to a cloud takes the subject from there and only issuer and audience from here, so trust and execution cannot drift apart when the definition moves to another runner.

The template understands two placeholders, `{{ workspaceIdentifier }}` and `{{ buildingBlockDefinitionUuid }}`; a template without placeholders is a fixed subject, which is what a runner minting one identity for all of its runs declares.

~> **Preview:** This resource is in preview. Breaking changes are possible without prior notice due to changes in the underlying [meshStack preview API](https://docs.meshcloud.io/api/technical-specifications#preview-endpoints) or due to changes in this provider. Please ensure you are running the latest version of the provider and report any bugs via [GitHub issues](https://github.com/meshcloud/terraform-provider-meshstack/issues) or via support@meshcloud.io.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "meshstack_building_block_runner" "example" {
  # Omit metadata entirely to read the shared runner meshStack hosts, which is also the runner a
  # building block definition uses when its version_spec.runner_ref is omitted.
  metadata = {
    uuid = meshstack_building_block_runner.example.metadata.uuid
  }
}

# Trust the runner in a cloud backplane: issuer and audience describe the runner and are known before
# any building block definition exists, while the subject is resolved per definition and read there.
locals {
  oidc_issuer  = data.meshstack_building_block_runner.example.spec.workload_identity_federation.issuer
  aws_audience = data.meshstack_building_block_runner.example.spec.workload_identity_federation.aws.audience
  aws_subject  = meshstack_building_block_definition.example.status.workload_identity_federation.subject
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `metadata` (Attributes) Metadata of the building block runner. Omit it to read the shared runner. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--metadata))

### Read-Only

- `ref` (Attributes) Reference to this runner, can be used as `version_spec.runner_ref` of a building block definition. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ref))
- `spec` (Attributes) Specification of the building block runner. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec))

<a id="nestedatt--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `metadata`

Optional:

- `uuid` (String) UUID of the runner to read. Defaults to `98520496-627d-43e6-82da-ce499179ff3f`, the shared runner meshStack hosts, which is also the runner a building block definition uses when its `version_spec.runner_ref` is omitted.

Read-Only:

- `created_on` (String) Timestamp when the runner was created (ISO 8601).
- `last_seen` (String) Timestamp when the runner last connected to meshStack (ISO 8601).
- `owned_by_workspace` (String) Identifier of the workspace that owns this runner.


<a id="nestedatt--ref"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ref`

Read-Only:

- `kind` (String) meshObject type, always `meshBuildingBlockRunner`.
- `uuid` (String) UUID (`metadata.uuid`) of `meshBuildingBlockRunner`.


<a id="nestedatt--spec"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String) Human-readable display name of the runner.
- `implementation_type` (String) Type of building block implementation this runner handles. One of: `TERRAFORM`, `GITHUB_WORKFLOW`, `GITLAB_PIPELINE`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_PIPELINE`, `MANUAL`, `ALL`.
- `is_self_hosted` (Boolean) Whether the runner is hosted by you rather than by meshStack.
- `restriction` (String) Visibility restriction of the runner. `PUBLIC` makes it available to all workspaces, `PRIVATE` to the owning workspace only.
- `workload_identity_federation` (Attributes) The identity scheme this runner declares. Null when the runner presents no identity of its own. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation))

<a id="nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.workload_identity_federation`

Read-Only:

- `aws` (Attributes) Workload identity federation values for AWS. Null when the runner does not federate with AWS. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--aws))
- `azure` (Attributes) Workload identity federation values for Azure. Null when the runner does not federate with Azure. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--azure))
- `gcp` (Attributes) Workload identity federation values for GCP. Null when the runner does not federate with GCP. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--gcp))
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL of the identity provider that issues tokens for this runner's building block runs. Trust it in your cloud backplane.
- `subject_template` (String) The template meshStack resolves into the subject claim of the tokens this runner presents, for example `system:serviceaccount:my-namespace:workspace.{{ workspaceIdentifier }}.buildingblockdefinition.{{ buildingBlockDefinitionUuid }}`. Two placeholders are available: `{{ workspaceIdentifier }}` (the identifier of the workspace owning the building block definition) and `{{ buildingBlockDefinitionUuid }}` (`metadata.uuid` of that definition). A template without placeholders is a fixed subject, which is what a runner minting one identity for all its runs declares. meshStack resolves the template per building block definition and reports the result as `meshstack_building_block_definition.<name>.status.workload_identity_federation.subject`.

<a id="nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--aws"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.workload_identity_federation.aws`

Read-Only:

- `audience` (String) Audience the federated identity token is issued for. Trust this value in your AWS backplane.
- `token_path` (String) Path the runner writes that token to.


<a id="nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--azure"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.workload_identity_federation.azure`

Read-Only:

- `audience` (String) Audience the federated identity token is issued for. Trust this value in your Azure backplane.
- `token_path` (String) Path the runner writes that token to.


<a id="nestedatt--spec--workload_identity_federation--gcp"></a>
### Nested Schema for `spec.workload_identity_federation.gcp`

Read-Only:

- `audience` (String) Audience the federated identity token is issued for. Trust this value in your GCP backplane.
- `token_path` (String) Path the runner writes that token to.
